 For Applicant : Ms. Sareena Khan, Advocate.
For State : Mr. Kalpesh Ruparel, Panel Lawyer.

This second application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of bail has been filed by the accused/applicant who has been arrested in connection with Crime No.471/2022 registered at Police Station Patna, Koriya for the offence under Sections 363, 366 (A), 368, 370 (4), 376 (2) (n),
506, 370 (A), 120-B & 34 of the IPC and Sections 4, 9 & 17 of the POCSO Act.

2. Prosecution case, in brief, is that the present applicant who was involved in a racket of women trafficking had abducted the minor prosecutrix and sent her to the co-accused Pawan, a resident of Haryana, who had sexually exploited her.
Therefore, the offence as aforesaid has been registered against the applicant.
It is pertinent to mention here that earlier bail application filed by the applicant was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 28.06.2023 passed in MCRC No.4507/2023.

sentences.text:

1 3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the accused/applicant is innocent and has been roped in a false case.

She submits that the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19214 learned trial Court has passed the order of rejection of bail on 15.03.2024 and thereafter victim and her father informed the trial Court regarding wrong investigation in the case and the trial Court also permitted for re-cross examination of the victim and her father.
In such circumstances, it is clear that the prosecutrix herself supports the case of the defence.
She also submits that applicant is languishing in jail since 12.12.2022.
Therefore, considering all these aspects, the applicant may be released on bail.
4. Per contra, learned State counsel vehemently opposes the prayer for bail.

He draws attention towards paragraph 5 of the victim's statement and submits that prosecutrix has categorically described the manner in which said crime has been committed and at para 9 she duly identified the applicant in chief-examination.

He also apprise this Court that chief examination of the victim was conducted on 10 th April, 2023, however, her cross-examination was not completed on same day,
therefore, she was called on 11.04.2023.
On that day also victim's cross-examination was not concluded up-till lunch hours by the defence lawyer and after the post-lunch session her cross-examination continued and completed.

Thereafter, on 15.03.2024 an application was preferred by the defence under Section 311 Cr.P.C. for recalling of cross-examination of the victim and her father on the ground that they have informed the Court that wrong investigation has been done.
Thereafter, the trial Court allowed the said application for recalling of cross-examination of the victim and her father.

Learned State counsel submits that it appears that the learned trial Court is not giving proper attention towards procedure and spirit of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 as Section 35 (2) of the said Act clearly says that the Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19214 repeatedly to testify in the court.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned State counsel lastly submits that this is case of human trafficking and sexual exploitation with the minor victim by the gang, therefore, present is not a fit case for grant of bail.
5.

Having regard to the aforesaid submissions and keeping in mind the fact that earlier bail application was rejected on merits further considering the gravity of offence and considering the the victim's evidence, I do not find present to be a good case for grant of bail.
6. Accordingly, the application is rejected.

Sd/-
(Deepak Kumar Tiwari) Judge Ajay Sanju (As Per Police Story Shushma) vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30407947/
